encryption.note: Host verdicts inferred by Claude from Lionel's published replies; every note links the replies it rests on. Lionel approves the wording. Verdicts: holds, questioned (his question is not yet answered), weak (his objection undercuts the claim as stated), duplicate (of another row), retired.

R1.note: The bound H(K) >= H(M) is the price of perfect secrecy only. Computational encryption needs a short key, even a constant-length one, so the cost argument does not bind. And entropy is cheap in nature.

R2.note: Why would the private key need to be inherited? The argument assumes it without saying why.

R4.note: Why is the eavesdropper's problem not a computational one just because the information is carried in molecules?

R5.note: Restates R1's Shannon-bound argument, so the objection to R1 applies here too.

C1.note: Humor is an edge case. Did nature invent it, or did humans? A joke has no precise decryption, and a plaintext has no unique encryption as a joke; it may have many, or none.
